[h2]More music[/h2]
Chris has spent more time on the project, working into the music tracks. We've started filling out more of the times of day, so now we have a daytime, evening and night track we're happy with.


There we go! Another month has flown by and the game is coming along nicely I'd say!

It makes such a big difference now that others are involved, and the quality is just improving constantly. Writing this post has made me very happy, being reminded that Hokko is becoming something really wonderful 🥰

Thanks for reading, and for your support! As always, let me know your thoughts in the comments, or in our Discord server!



Take care of yourselves!
[i]from Robert[/i]

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #5
notes.content:
[h3]We’ve been incredibly busy bees these past couple of months! Robert from Wonderscope Games has the latest scoop for you… [/h3]

[h2]Dialog & Camera[/h2]
I reworked the dialog system so that more than two people can have a conversation in the world! In the conversation files I added functionality that can switch between characters at different points in the dialog, as well as functions for checking if characters are nearby and triggering different conversation.

Along with this update, I worked into the camera so that it frames characters better and moves between them depending on who is talking. All this stuff will come into use in the next months when more of the intro to the game and character dialog is written.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GK4lCOk.gif[/img]

[h2]Town Center Unlocks[/h2]
Over the course of the game you'll unlock different buildings in the town center. This month I implemented the parts required to get this working; where parts of the town center will change visually when a new building is unlocked. These buildings will be unlocked when you've become friends with their owner and they've decided to move to town.

[h2]New Character Moving-in Flow[/h2]
In Hokko life, based on your actions and the type of town you build, you'll "unlock" new visitors and potential residents! Up until now when a character was unlocked, they'd start appearing in the world, wandering around a bit aimlessly at certain times of day. This felt really strange, as characters you didn't know would start showing up, and you'd often miss new animals because they'd be in an area you didn't visit for example. The initial story for this was that they'd arrive at the train station, wander around a bit and then head home; but without actually seeing their arrival, it just meant they were in the world randomly.

With the new pub/restaurant location added to the town center, visitors to your town will now appear here, either during lunch time or the evening. Once you've unlocked a new character they'll appear here and you can then talk to and befriend them. Once you've built them a house and they have moved to town they'll start wandering around and existing in the world. Setting things up this way means that you'll have a lot lower chance of missing potential residents, as they'll be at a main location at set times. It also allows for some really cozy evening chat dialog!

Once you've become good enough friends with a character, after chatting to them when they visit, you'll get the option to ask them to move in. Doing so will put them in a moving in "queue". Whenever you build a new house you can choose which character you'd like to move into that house from this list. Previously you would need to have a vacant house ready in order to ask a character to move to town, which, I felt, could cause frustration. Imagine having a character that only visits every few weeks, on a Tuesday, at lunch time, that you've finally gotten close enough with to ask them to move in, only to find you don't have a house ready! You'd have to wait until their next visit to ask them to move in, which I felt would be annoying.

[h2]Moving Boxes[/h2]
When a character moves to town they'll now bring with them a bunch of items for their home and will decorate the walls and flooring in their own style. As their friend, you'll help them move in by unpacking their items and placing them where you'd like in the room. This way you get to design everyone's home, but still retain some of their personal charm (unless you hate their style, then you can just sell their stuff...! 🤫)

[h2]World Redesign[/h2]
I went through the whole world of Hokko this month and redesigned it completely. 

The old world was too flat with not much variation and didn't have distinct enough areas. Alongside this, it wasn't built with progression in mind, and so the player could easily reach all areas from the beginning of the game. 

The new world comes from a paper plan I doodled, thinking about how the town would flow, allowing for different area types and how they'd all connect.

Here are some shots of the new levels:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/1097fd99bd27bbb07a4f9630ee694c38ae40177f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a5af45b0f72e3de4fc308e37e726f2613e75e0d6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/ab2badebed072cae4e14fe92ad8d890bb7fae066.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/d12f5d11f249b911e096e3a9ba3b96d92c442d44.png[/img]

[h2]The Bomb[/h2]
Now that parts of the world are locked-off, you'll need to use both your design skills and crafting in order to progress. Several of the areas require you to design special items to access them, and others need... a bomb...!

Now there's a craftable bomb in the game (with placeholder graphics right now) which you can use to blast your way through areas blocked by rubble and rocks; for example when trying to get into the mine:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/r0DUsCI.gif[/img]

[h2]Clothing [/h2]
Eva's hopped on board this month and has been busy working away on clothing items. These have ranged from jackets, to shoes, skirts, pants and more!

Here is a very small selection of some of the pieces she's created:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/adb6d847074120de851843579f05f408fc1d1048.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/74ca571b7c1e1bd25c05fbb9d968aef109a0aa7a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Town Center Assets[/h2]
The artists over at Team17 have been working away on assets for the town center too, primarily updating the buildings. 

This month we got a new train station and builder’s hut!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/52a0c523a40f08d2d78b0debc4371c3b2748407e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/b7222268b98e36cbe252218e2de9fde23855c50d.png[/img]

There was also a rather lovely tree finished!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/09ff5c4579915608e18ad7e0bb580d1bc6366ada.png[/img]

So there we have it! 

With more hands on the project a lot more gets done in a month, as you can no doubt see!

I hope you're all keeping well, let me know your thoughts in the comments, or in our Discord server!

Speak soon,
[i]from Robert[/i]

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #4
notes.content:
[h2]What’s been happening with Hokko Life development? Here’s an update from Robert at Wonderscope Games![/h2]


As another month races by the summer fills the days with lovely sunsets, late night BBQs and lake swimming, and it's time for a new devlog about Hokko!

[h3]Expressions[/h3]
I updated the Avatar's head shader to allow for expressions! With the new Avatar head mesh we set up the texturing so that details on the face would be handled with different textures; this means I can swap out a mouth or eye texture to provide different expressions. I edited the head shader this month to work with this and added three new emotions to the game: happy, straining, and winking.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3muLnuK.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/da353c7c3b26d08734381ee1cbb05d56969e570e.png[/img]

[h3]Energy[/h3]
I've been contemplating for a little while adding a system similar to stamina to the game. I decided to get a first implementation of this in this month to get a feel for whether or not it made sense or felt right. I gave the player an amount of energy that they consume when performing tasks like chopping down trees or mining. Once you've depleted your energy you'll need to take a short break to recharge some of it. You'll only replenish a small amount, so you'll need to grab some food or rest if you want to do a lot more work, but it will never empty completely stopping you from working altogether. I wanted to get a nice balance, rewarding players for preparing before they go off resource gathering but not penalize them if they run out of energy.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3k6Lqu4.gif[/img]
[i]Running out of energy means you'll need to catch your breath before continuing to work[/i]

We'll see if it stays or not, but it allows me to pace the activities in the game better; gives something else you can do with farmed produce; and can add some interesting gameplay to exploring the world.

As part of this energy prototype work I added jumping to the game! This will enable you to get over small gaps in the world and consumes a bit of energy. With this I'm thinking that you will unlock ways of building structures that cross these gaps as you progress later in the game, making traversal of the world smoother. One of these structures is....

[h3]Bridges! [/h3]

I added a bridge design blueprint to the game, which allows players to design their own bridges and then place them out in the world! 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3qZOOlv.gif[/img]
[i]Placing a bridge I designed[/i]

[h3]Farming[/h3]
Farming was one of the main focuses for this month, with the plan to expand a bit upon the simple base that was there already.

I added fertilizer to the game; it's craftable from different resources in the world and when placed on tilled soil it will increase the chances of a crop being higher quality. High quality crops can be sold for money and are sometimes requested by characters in the game. Fertilizer will be active on a patch of soil for a set amount of time and anything planted there within that duration will have it's chances tweaked.

I added templates for two new characters to the game. One is the farmer character, who will act as your introduction to farming, and will provide you with crafting recipes for your first equipment. After you've gotten under way they'll sell you different types of seeds, and some crafting recipes for things that will make your farming life easier, such as...

[h3]Sprinklers! [/h3]

I added two types of sprinkler to the game, one that waters in a ring and one that waters in a line. Once you've purchased the crafting recipe from the farmer, these can be crafted with a few resources and will make your farming life a lot easier!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/w8VQLHi.gif[/img]

The other character I added to the game will provide you with challenges for farming, requesting numbers of produce within a certain amount of time; to enable this I expanded upon the request system to allow for deadlines.

[h3]Gardening[/h3]
As part of farming I added the concept of "gardening" to the game. This essentially allows you to plant flowers and trees in the world from seeds. Previously they'd grow by themselves in various locations, but the player couldn't really move them around or plant them where they wanted. Now you can dig a hole in the ground and plant seeds that will grow over time. Trees and flowers can be planted in this way, and unlike crops they don't need watering and can be dug up and moved around as they're growing (you'll need to chop down trees when they get big though!).

This addition lets players have more control over their town and its appearance and allows you to set up areas for growing flowers for crafting too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/59ab278bdbc8df19174de95f2712f24c6a33de33.png[/img]
[i]Baby plants![/i]

[h3]UI Stuff[/h3]
With the new Farmer character providing you with seeds and other items for purchase I decided to build a system in the UI for displaying more detailed information on a selected item. Seeds need to show how long they take to grow, for example, and craftable items need to show what resources they require. As this was a common requirement in a lot places in the game, I built a reusable system that I can use anywhere to display this information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/a5533f11d957b6299d2ff74db4b51eba4b94d55a.png[/img]
[i]The styles are very WIP at the moment, but you can see the info panel on the right showing information about the seeds[/i]

[h3]Piece Packs[/h3]
As you progress in the game you'll unlock more pieces you can use to design items with. This month I implemented what was needed for this to work and introduced something I'm calling "Piece Packs". Piece packs are collections of pieces you can use when designing and are unlocked as a bundle for a set price; I thought unlocking pieces in this way would be a lot more fun too! 

With Piece Packs being purchasable, I updated the Design Tool to show these packs as groups and added filter buttons allowing the player to show and hide different packs based on the materials needed.

And there we have it, all of the stuff that got done in June!

I hope you've been keeping safe and still enjoying the sunny weather.

Speak soon!
[i]from Robert[/i]

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
[h2]Here’s a fresh update on development from Robert at Wonderscope Games![/h2]

Let's get stuck into devlog #3!

[b][h3]Fishing[/h3][/b]The majority of this month's work has been focused on working into and expanding on the fishing gameplay. 

I thought I'd walk you through how fishing works in Hokko Life in order to show off changes made this month! 

After starting the inventory re-write last month, I was able to add bait to the game! This can be attached to a fishing rod you have equipped and will alter your chances of catching certain fish. Bait can be crafted from different resources found in the world, once you've unlocked their crafting recipes.

Right clicking on a type of bait in your backpack will give you the option of attaching it to your fishing rod:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/f1APGdb.gif[/img]

Once your bait and hook are in the water it's a case of waiting for a fish to spot them. A fish will take a few nibbles of the bait before being hooked.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Itk6tmU.gif[/img]

When the fish takes the last bite and the action UI pops up, you have a short window of time to press ‘Interact’ to hook the fish. 

This will start the fishing mini game!

The aim of the fishing mini game is to keep the fish inside the ring until it reaches the goal line. The fish has a mind of its own and will try and swim away, so you'll need to position your rod left and right, and press the interact button to reel the fish back into the ring. 

If the fish is outside of the ring for too long, it'll get away and you'll fail the mini game.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Cm1YUD6.gif[/img]

There's also a chance a chest will appear during the mini game. If you steer the fish through this chest it'll pop open and give you a random reward!

This month I tried out a "diorama" look for the fishing mini game, building a quick little scene to make the game cuter and more appealing. It was a boring rectangle before and I like this cuter direction. Depending on where you're fishing the diorama will change in appearance too!

[b][h3]Fishing Challenges[/h3][/b]I added fishing challenges to the game this month, these will unlock after you've been fishing a little while and offer a weekly challenge for players to get bonus rewards.

These challenges are generated once an in-game week and require you to catch a certain number of fish within a time limit. This can either be a specific fish, or any fish, and the time limit is adjusted based on the rarity of the fish, as well as if there are any nearby. A bunch of things happen behind the scenes too, making sure that you have a chance of winning the challenge; but don't worry, if you fail you can always go back for a retry!

I wanted to get more variation in for the challenges, but just getting them set up and working in the first place took a lot longer than expected this month, so I had to settle with just one type for now. The system's there now for future challenge types to be added in the future at least!

[b][h3]Avatar Updates[/h3][/b]I spent some more time with the avatar this month, working into the animation system, how equipping and un-equipping tools works behind the scenes among other things. The goal with these changes was primarily to make the system less buggy, as well as improve the overall appearance. Simple things like adding an acceleration to the player to make the transition from standing to running look nicer, as well as adding equip animation variations to fit the different ways the player can hold an item.

I worked into some of the animations too, improving their weighting and timing. As last month's goal was to just get animations in, it was nice to spend a few hours improving them.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/QhkTbDH.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Vb6N22Q.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/REHaLWR.gif[/img]

I also spent a little time playing with the face and head shape, getting it closer to something I'm happy with.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GSNGtVG.png[/img]

I added the other clothing base meshes to the game for pants, sweater and skirt and made sure they showed up in the shop for purchase. I removed all the old clothing items, as they'll need to be replaced, as well as all the old avatar assets (deleting old ugly stuff feels so good!)

I also tweaked all the old hair styles a little bit so they fit on the new head mesh. They'll need further tweaking to get them perfect, but they looked horrific before and I had to do something about it, haha!

And that, I think, is everything I worked on this month! Feels like quite a lot when I write it all out and add pictures!

Hope you're all keeping well and enjoying the start of summer as much as possible!

Speak soon!
[i]from Robert[/i]

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #2
notes.content:
[b]Want to know what’s been going on with Hokko Life? Robert from Wonderscope Games is here to keep you up to date with the latest dev blog![/b]


It continues to amaze me how quickly time goes by now; that we're in May already is just crazy!
I hope you, your family, and your community are all doing alright during this time we find ourselves in.

So what got done this past month?


[h3]Publisher stuff[/h3]
This month was the first proper month working with Team17. We've been having quite a few discussions and Skype calls setting things up and figuring out how we move forward. Team17 are going to be helping with some development stuff as well as publishing, so we've been getting together plans for how development will look, and I've been discussing with them my vision for the game both in terms of design and art. I put together a Game Design Document for them to outline all the features of the game and how they work, so that there's a reference there for anyone hopping onto the project.
In combination with this, I've started booking time with myself in the form of some kind of mini meetings, where I focus entirely on thinking about design, story and art for the game. It's very easy to ignore these types of things, as the allure of working directly on the game is very strong, but with a few others joining the project I decided that for everyone's benefit I needed to dedicate some time to this stuff. I've only had a few meetings so far, but they're already having a great effect on how comfortable I am with the game.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/LVTRgbp.gif[/img]

[h3]New avatar[/h3]
Content-wise I worked on getting the new avatar into the game this month. The model was created by the talented Hanna Kime (check her stuff out here: https://www.artstation.com/quickhanna) a little while back, and I had this month down for getting it in-game. I spent some time getting used to how rigging and skinning works in Blender (I was using Modo before) and then got the new avatar mesh set up ready for animation. I spent a week or so on this, followed by another week blocking out all the animations in the game. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WHHoSvD.gif[/img]

The goal with the animations was to set them up to keep the game working, with the intention to work into the polish for them next month. I quickly got clothing onto the character too, and this will also be fixed up properly next month too but it felt a lot better than having a naked character running around!


[img]https://i.imgur.com/gXbTAqZ.gif[/img]

And that's more or less it for now! Next month will focus on working into the quality of the avatar, bringing in the other base clothing meshes and improving the animations. There will be some time spent working into fishing too, making the experience a bit deeper and more refined.

Speak to you soon!

Robert

notes.title: Hokko Life Devlog #1
notes.content:
[h1]Check out this devblog from Robert at Wonderscope for the latest updates for Hokko Life![/h1]

Well well well, what an exciting month April was for Hokko!

We announced our partnership with Team17 and made some epic updates to Hokko Life!

[h3]Art updates[/h3]At the start of the month I got stuck into updating the rocks in the game. Previously they’d all been colour variations of one basic rock, but now they have a distinct look depending on what type of ore they contain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/890d1acecdfa9e8643f7008004a314dc31788bc8.png[/img]
[i]Mine Rocks[/i]


There's now a bunch of new fish! I spent some time thinking about the style for the fish (and the rest of the game) and how I'd like them to look. I went through some iterations and decided on a clean and stylized look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/9a77d4fb95297a7362dd79f717253379013724df.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36794188/9b43c750c69447353251e8e49826cd12c8867a11.png[/img]
[i]New Fish[/i]

Following on from updating the style of the fish, I wanted to tackle a building and update it to a newer style. For this I took the Workshop, one of the oldest assets in the game, and gave it a tidy-up. Cleaning up the texture and making it fit the newer style.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/90DQ4kh.gif[/img]
[i]Updated Workshop[/i]

I looked at the grass in the game, spending some time improving the ground texture as well as making some new 3D grass that sticks up and adds depth. I think this all makes the world feel richer and really brings the quality level up a notch.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/KmWJ9gc.gif[/img]
[i]New Grass[/i]

[h3]Design Anywhere[/h3]Near the end of the month I started working on letting players be able to edit the design of objects in the world, just by running up to them and interacting with them. Up until now the player would need to go all the way to the workshop to edit a design and would need to have that object in their backpack to do so. Now, if you see something you'd like to edit, you can edit it from anywhere in the world. 

I'm going to continue looking at ways like this to make the game more immediate and fun, trying to remove some of the frustrating stuff that often gets in the way.

[h3]Steam[/h3]I updated my process for making builds of the game and hooked it up to Steam so that I can send builds to Steam from within the Unity Editor. I'd been using Discord up until this month to send builds to my composer and others, but now it's all on Steam! Woo!

That's it for now. I hope you're all keeping well and safe.

Thanks as always for your continued support!

Robert
